  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "incident_inefficiency_reasons",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "incident_category",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The type of affected asset/system is a constitutive aspect of what an incident's inefficiency reason is about (what kind of thing failed)."
    },
    {
      "name": "failure_mode",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "How the thing failed is a core aspect of the reason an incident is inefficient to resolve; a genuine part of the concept."
    },
    {
      "name": "issue_nature",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "restatement",
      "rationale": "Hardware/software/connectivity classification substantially overlaps with both incident_category (asset) and failure_mode (connectivity_failure, performance_degradation appear verbatim), largely restating those facets rather than adding a distinct aspect."
    },
    {
      "name": "requires_physical_intervention",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Whether physical action is needed is an aspect of what makes resolution inefficient (drives handling effort), a legitimate constitutive facet."
    },
    {
      "name": "recurrence_signal",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Recurrence is directly named in the query ('recurring issues') and is a constitutive aspect of the inefficiency reason."
    },
    {
      "name": "scope_context",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The breadth/impact scope (individual vs shared/infrastructure) is an aspect of the incident that shapes resolution effort; a valid facet, though it partly correlates with incident_category."
    },
    {
      "name": "self_resolved_by_assignee",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "external_predictor",
      "rationale": "This describes a resolution OUTCOME/handling behavior, not a constitutive aspect of the inefficiency reason itself; it is an effect/observable predictor rather than a part-of facet."
    },
    {
      "name": "urgency_signal",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "external_predictor",
      "rationale": "Urgency/priority is an attribute governing prioritization (already present as priority) rather than a constitutive part of why resolution is inefficient; it is an external driver, not a facet of the reason."
    }
  ],
  "facet_columns": [
    "incident_category",
    "failure_mode",
    "requires_physical_intervention",
    "recurrence_signal",
    "scope_context"
  ],
  "non_facet_columns": [
    "issue_nature",
    "self_resolved_by_assignee",
    "urgency_signal"
  ],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.5,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.6,
  "rationale": "Several columns are genuine part-of facets of the inefficiency-reason concept (what failed, how it failed, physical intervention, recurrence, scope). However mutual exclusivity is weakened: issue_nature largely restates incident_category and failure_mode (sharing connectivity_failure and performance_degradation values), and scope_context correlates with incident_category. Two columns are not facets at all: self_resolved_by_assignee is a resolution outcome and urgency_signal is an external prioritization driver, both effects/predictors rather than constitutive aspects. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the retained facets cover asset, failure mode, physicality, recurrence, and scope, but overlaps mean effective distinct coverage is thinner than the column count suggests."
}
